---
title: "Where public money goes"
description: "How money comes in to the State, and what it is spent on, from health and pensions down to hospitals and schools."
---

Every year the State collects money through taxes such as income tax, VAT and corporation tax, through PRSI, and through fees and other income. That money goes into a common pool, which pays for public services, welfare payments and interest on government debt. The chart below follows the money from where it comes from to what it is spent on.

{{< chart public-finances-flows >}}

Social protection is the largest area of spending. It covers State pensions, jobseeker and disability payments, child benefit and housing supports. Health and education come next.

The chart below breaks each area of spending into its parts, such as hospitals within health or primary and secondary schools within education. Select an area to see what it is made up of.

{{< chart public-finances-by-purpose >}}

These figures cover all of general government, including local authorities, the HSE and other public bodies, and are measured the same way across the EU. They are arranged by purpose rather than by government department, so a single department's budget can appear across several areas.
